\extable{300_q37_t1}

A person with a taxable income of \$90 000 pays $25.8\%$ of that income in tax (excluding any levies).

What is the value of $X$ in the table?

solutions.latex:
Tax on $\$90\,000$ is $25.8\%$ of the income.
$$\$90\,000\times 0.258 = \$23\,220$$
The income above $\$78\,800$ is taxed at $X$ cents per dollar.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Income over } \$78\,800 &= 90\,000-78\,800\\ &= \$11\,200\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Tax on this part} &= 23\,220-18\,292\\ &= \$4928\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}11\,200\times X &= 4928\\ X &= \dfrac{4928}{11\,200}\\ &= 0.44\end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ X = 44 \text{ cents}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the amount to which $X$ cents applies, or equivalent merit
Calculates $25.8\%$ of $90\,000$, or equivalent merit

\extable{15_q33_t1}

Marcus earned an annual gross salary of \$109 200 and had allowable deductions of \$8700.

Calculate Marcus's total tax payable, including the Medicare Levy which is charged at 2% of taxable income.

solutions.latex:
Taxable income is gross salary less deductions.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Taxable income} &= 109\,200 - 8700 \\ &= \$100\,500 \end{aligned}$$
From the tax table, income tax payable is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Income tax} &= 5092 + 0.325(100\,500 - 45\,000) \\ &= \$23\,129.50 \end{aligned}$$
The Medicare levy is
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Medicare levy} &= 2\% \times 100\,500 \\ &= \$2010 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total tax payable} &= 23\,129.50 + 2010 \\ &= \$25\,139.50 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Correct taxable income and income tax payable, or taxable income and Medicare levy, or correct tax payable with one mistake, or equivalent merit
Only one correct

6053.stem:
In a typical week Kim works 36 hours and is paid \$42 per hour.

In the 2025–2026 financial year, Kim took 4 weeks annual leave and received a leave loading of $17.5\%$ of 4 weeks pay.

In the same year, Kim also had allowable deductions totalling \$4800. Use 1 year = 52 weeks.

solutions.latex:
Weekly pay:
$$42 \times 36 = \$1512$$
Taxable income is annual pay plus leave loading, less deductions:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Taxable income} &= 1512 \times 52 + 4 \times 1512 \times 17.5\% - 4800 \\ &= \$74\,882.40 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Deducts 4800 from an annual income, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Tax payable on the taxable income:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Tax} &= 4288 + 0.3(74\,882 - 45\,000) \\ &= \$13\,252.60 \end{aligned}$$
Medicare levy:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Levy} &= 2\% \times 74\,882.40 \\ &= \$1497.65 \end{aligned}$$
Total tax:
$$\begin{aligned} 13\,252.60 + 1497.65 &= \$14\,750.25 \end{aligned}$$
Tax withheld (PAYG):
$$383 \times 52 = \$19\,916$$
PAYG is greater than the total tax, so Kim receives a refund.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Refund} &= 19\,916 - 14\,750.25 \\ &= \$5165.75 \\ &\approx \$5166 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the total tax payable, or equivalent merit
Finds the tax payable without Medicare levy, or equivalent merit

\extable{5834_q31_t1}

At the end of the 2024–2025 financial year, Alex's tax payable was \$47\,420, excluding the Medicare levy.

What was Alex's taxable income?

solutions.latex:
Tax of $\$47\,420$ lies in the $37\%$ bracket, which has base tax $\$31\,288$ on income over $\$135\,000$.
$$\begin{aligned} \$47\,420 &= \$31\,288 + 0.37(\text{taxable income} - \$135\,000) \\ \$16\,132 &= 0.37(\text{taxable income} - \$135\,000) \\ \$43\,600 &= \text{taxable income} - \$135\,000 \\ \text{taxable income} &= \$43\,600 + \$135\,000 \\ &= \$178\,600 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Provides evidence of using $0.37$ in a tax calculation, or equivalent merit
Shows evidence of using correct line in the table, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:

Finds the income tax or the Medicare levy, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:

Compare with the tax payable:

The table shows the individual income tax rates in Australia for the 2022–23 financial year.

\extable{717_q21_t1}

Cameron is a teacher and his gross annual income is \$108 000. He paid a total of \$26 200 in Pay As You Go (PAYG) tax during the 2022–23 financial year. His tax deductions include the purchase of teaching resources valued at \$342 and teacher union fees of \$674. Cameron must also pay a Medicare levy of 2% of his taxable income.

Given that Cameron paid \$26 200 in PAYG tax, determine whether he will receive a tax refund or owe money to the Australian Taxation Office and if he owes the ATO by how much.

solutions.latex:
Deductions are subtracted from gross income.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Taxable income}&=108\,000-(342+674)\\&=\$106\,984\end{aligned}$$
This income lies in the bracket above \$45 000, so
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Tax payable}&=5902+(106\,984-45\,000)\times 0.325\\&=\$26\,046.80\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Medicare levy}&=2\%\times 106\,984\\&=\$2139.68\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Total taxes}&=26\,046.80+2139.68\\&=\$28\,186.48\end{aligned}$$
Cameron has paid \$26 200, which is less than \$28 186.48.
$$\therefore\ \text{Cameron owes the ATO } \$1986.48.$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds the total tax including the Medicare levy, or equivalent merit
Finds the tax payable on the taxable income, or equivalent merit
Finds the taxable income, or equivalent merit

6504.stem: James has a gross income of \$65 800 for the year, and claims tax deductions of \$650.

parts.latex:
Use the tax rates below to find his tax payable.

\exfigure{1266_q26_1}

James also must pay the Medicare levy, which is $2\%$ of his taxable income.

Find the total amount of tax and Medicare levy that James must pay.

solutions.latex:
Taxable income is gross income less deductions.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Taxable income} &= 65\,800 - 650 \\ &= \$65\,150 \end{aligned}$$
This lies in the bracket starting at $\$45\,000$, so
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Tax payable} &= 5092 + 0.325 \times (65\,150 - 45\,000) \\ &= \$11\,640.75 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Finds taxable income and attempts to use the correct tax bracket from the table, or equivalent merit
Finds taxable income, or attempts to find tax payable, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The Medicare levy is $2\%$ of taxable income.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Medicare levy} &= 2\% \times 65\,150 \\ &= \$1303 \end{aligned}$$
The total is the tax payable from part (a) plus the levy.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total} &= 11\,640.75 + 1303 \\ &= \$12\,943.75 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answer
Attempts to find Medicare levy, or equivalent merit
